subjects.label: Decks and archetypes
subjects.description: The named decks and archetypes players run, love or hate, and the meta they form, including calls for a theme to be buffed or for the meta to change; not the general mechanics of summoning.

subjects.label: Banlist and formats
subjects.description: Which cards are forbidden or limited, whether the list follows the TCG, calls to ban a specific card, and requests for other formats or queues such as Genesys, tag duels or unranked; not balance complaints that name no card.

subjects.label: Hand traps and the coin toss
subjects.description: Maxx C, Ash Blossom, Nibiru and the rest of the negation game, going first or second, being negated on every play and bricking; not the length of the opponent's turn, which has its own row.

subjects.label: Long opponent turns
subjects.description: Sitting through an opponent's solitaire turn while they build a full board in one go, alt-tabbing until it is over, and the one-turn combo as a spectacle; not hand traps or the coin toss.

subjects.label: Gems and pay to win
subjects.description: Earning gems, quests that stop paying out, pack pulls, dismantling cards for craft points, and whether a competitive deck is reachable without a credit card; not cosmetics.

subjects.label: Konami
subjects.description: Reviews that address the company by name, cursing or crediting it for the state of the game; not complaints about the game that never name it.

subjects.label: The anime and childhood
subjects.description: Playground memories of the card game, the anime and its summon chants, players returning after a decade away, and whether you need to know the franchise at all; not the game's own story mode.

subjects.label: Card text and effect design
subjects.description: The paragraphs of effect text on a card, cards written to be unreadable, and rules terms a newcomer does not know; not the tutorial itself.

subjects.label: Rage and addiction
subjects.description: Tilting, broken mice and monitors, raised blood pressure, suffering, and being unable to stop queueing anyway; not the mood or atmosphere of the game itself.
